rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while protecting the workload's hot numeric loops (fannkuch, spectral-norm, n-body, partialsums dominate runtime). Cheap, low-risk passes get the strongest pull: SUB (arithmetic substitution) and IBR (indirect branch) at high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with low cost weights, since these benchmarks are branch- and arithmetic-dense so those passes yield real resistance for minimal overhead; SPLIT and ICALL follow to fragment the tiny function bodies and add call indirection, boosting binary diversity across seeds. BCF is deliberately suppressed (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights) because bogus control flow bloats a 909-byte text section and taxes inner loops heavily relative to its modest security benefit; FLA stays moderate for the same reason — flattening the small hot kernels would cost more runtime than it hides. IGV remains enabled with moderate weights since it protects the few globals cheaply. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay low, keeping the selector conservative on the correctness-critical paths that round 1 already validated.
